newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SOCCER FANS ON TRIAL AFTER AJAX KILLING.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SOCCER FANS ON TRIAL AFTER AJAX KILLING.

text.p: A group of Feyenoord Rotterdam soccer fans appeared before a Dutch court on Tuesday, charged with taking part in the fatal beating of a rival supporter.
A spokeswoman at the heavily guarded court in Haarlem, 15 miles west of Amsterdam, said the trial of the 14 young men would last at least a week.
Carlo Picornie, a hardcore Ajax Amsterdam fan and known ringleader, was clubbed to death in March in a pre-arranged clash between two rival soccer gangs on wasteland outside Amsterdam.
Police said the showdown involved hundreds of armed fans. Eyewitnesses likened the scene near a busy motorway to a seal cull.
The spokeswoman said the prosecution had so far asked the court to hand down a five-year prison sentence to a 20-year-old Rotterdam man, accused of direct involvement in 35-year-old Picornie's death.
It has called for lesser sentences for two other defendants.
The rivalry between Rotterdam-based Feyenoord and Ajax Amsterdam reflects a deep cultural divide between the Netherlands' two biggest cities.
Dutch government ministers were swift to condemn the incident. In an attempt to combat soccer violence, clubs are considering introducing supporter identity cards next season.
